verses.zh: 看哪，我的仆人―我所扶持所拣选、心里所喜悦的！我已将我的灵赐给他；他必将公理传给外邦。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “Here is my servant whom I support,my chosen one in whom I take pleasure.I have placed my Spirit on him;he will make just decrees[NOTE:2] for the nations.[NOTE:3]
notes: Verses 1-7 contain the first of Isaiah’s “servant songs,” which describe the ministry of a special, ideal servant who accomplishes God’s purposes for Israel and the nations. This song depicts the servant as a just king who brings justice to the earth and relief for the oppressed. The other songs appear in 49:1-13; 50:4-11; and 52:13-53:12.
Heb “he will bring out justice” (cf. ASV, NASB, NRSV).
Like the ideal king portrayed in Isa 11:1-9, the servant is energized by the divine spirit and establishes justice on the earth.

verses.zh: 他不喧嚷，不扬声，也不使街上听见他的声音。
verses.en: He will not cry out or shout;he will not publicize himself in the streets.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he will not cause his voice to be heard in the street.”

verses.zh: 压伤的芦苇，他不折断；将残的灯火，他不吹灭。他凭真实将公理传开。
verses.en: A crushed reed he will not break,a dim wick he will not extinguish;[NOTE:1] he will faithfully make just decrees.[NOTE:2]
notes: The “crushed reed” and “dim wick” symbolize the weak and oppressed who are on the verge of extinction.
Heb “faithfully he will bring out justice” (cf. NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 他不灰心，也不丧胆，直到他在地上设立公理；海岛都等候他的训诲。
verses.en: He will not grow dim or be crushed[NOTE:1] before establishing justice on the earth;the coastlands[NOTE:2] will wait in anticipation for his decrees.”[NOTE:3]
notes: For rhetorical effect the terms used to describe the “crushed (רָצַץ, ratsats) reed” and “dim (כָּהָה, kahah) wick” in v. 3 are repeated here.
Or “islands” (NIV); NLT “distant lands beyond the sea.”
Or “his law” (KJV, ASV, NASB, NIV84) or “his instruction” (NLT) or “his teaching” (NIV11).

verses.zh: 创造诸天，铺张穹苍，将地和地所出的一并铺开，赐气息给地上的众人，又赐灵性给行在其上之人的　神耶和华，他如此说：
verses.en: This is what the true God,[NOTE:1] the Lord, says—the one who created the sky and stretched it out,the one who fashioned the earth and everything that lives on it,[NOTE:2] the one who gives breath to the people on it,and life to those who live on it:[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the God.” The definite article here indicates distinctiveness or uniqueness.
Heb “and its offspring” (so NASB); NIV84 “all that comes out of it”; NIV11 “all that springs from it.”
Heb “and spirit [i.e., “breath”] to the ones walking in it” (NAB, NASB, and NRSV all similar).

verses.zh: 我―耶和华凭公义召你，必搀扶你的手，保守你，使你作众民的中保（中保：原文是约），作外邦人的光，
verses.en: “I, the Lord, officially commission you;[NOTE:1] I take hold of your hand.I protect you[NOTE:2] and make you a covenant mediator for people[NOTE:3] and a light[NOTE:4] to the nations,[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “call you in righteousness.” The pronoun “you” is masculine singular, referring to the servant. See the note at 41:2.
The translation assumes the verb is derived from the root נָצַר (natsar, “protect”). Some prefer to derive it from the root יָצַר (yatsar, “form”).

Heb “a covenant of people.” A person cannot literally be a covenant; בְּרִית (berit) is probably metonymic here, indicating a covenant mediator. The precise identity of עָם (ʿam, “people”) is uncertain. In v. 5 עָם refers to mankind, and the following reference to “nations” also favors this. But in 49:8, where the phrase בְּרִית עָם occurs again, Israel seems to be in view.
Light here symbolizes deliverance from bondage and oppression; note the parallelism in 49:6b and in 51:4-6.
Or “the Gentiles” (so KJV, ASV, NIV); the same Hebrew word can be translated “nations” or “Gentiles” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 开瞎子的眼，领被囚的出牢狱，领坐黑暗的出监牢。
verses.en: to open blind eyes,[NOTE:1] to release prisoners[NOTE:2] from dungeons,those who live in darkness from prisons.
notes: This does not refer to literal physical healing of the blind. As the next two lines suggest, this refers metonymically to freeing captives from their dark prisons where their eyes have grown unaccustomed to light.

This does not refer to hardened, dangerous criminals, who would have been executed for their crimes in ancient Near Eastern society. This verse refers to political prisoners or victims of social injustice.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华，这是我的名；我必不将我的荣耀归给假神，也不将我的称赞归给雕刻的偶像。
verses.en: “I am the Lord! That is my name!I will not share my glory with anyone elseor the praise due me with idols.

verses.zh: 看哪，先前的事已经成就，现在我将新事说明，这事未发以先，我就说给你们听。
verses.en: Look, my earlier predictive oracles have come to pass;[NOTE:1] now I announce new events.Before they begin to occur,I reveal them to you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the former things, look, they have come.”

Heb “before they sprout up, I cause you to hear.” The pronoun “you” is plural, referring to the people of Israel. In this verse “the former things” are the Lord’s earlier predictive oracles which have come to pass, while “the new things” are predicted events that have not yet begun to take place. “The former things” are earlier events in Israel’s history which God announced beforehand, such as the Exodus (see 43:16-18). “The new things” are the predictions about the servant (42:1-7). and may also include Cyrus’ conquests (41:25-27).

verses.zh: 航海的和海中所有的，海岛和其上的居民，都当向耶和华唱新歌，从地极赞美他。
verses.en: Sing to the Lord a brand new song!Praise him[NOTE:1] from the horizon of the earth,you who go down to the sea and everything that lives in it,[NOTE:2] you coastlands[NOTE:3] and those who live there.
notes: Heb “his praise.” The phrase stands parallel to “new song” in the previous line.
Heb “and its fullness”; NASB, NIV “and all that is in it.”
Or “islands” (NASB, NIV); NLT “distant coastlands.”

verses.zh: 旷野和其中的城邑，并基达人居住的村庄都当扬声；西拉的居民当欢呼，在山顶上呐喊。
verses.en: Let the wilderness and its cities shout out,the towns where the nomads of Kedar live.Let the residents of Sela shout joyfully;let them shout loudly from the mountaintops.

verses.zh: 他们当将荣耀归给耶和华，在海岛中传扬他的颂赞。
verses.en: Let them give the Lord the honor he deserves;[NOTE:1] let them praise his deeds in the coastlands.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Let them ascribe to the Lord glory.”
Heb “and his praise in the coastlands [or “islands”] let them declare.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必像勇士出去，必像战士激动热心，要喊叫，大声呐喊，要用大力攻击仇敌。
verses.en: The Lord emerges like a hero,like a warrior he inspires himself for battle;[NOTE:1] he shouts, yes, he yells,he shows his enemies his power.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like a man of war he stirs up zeal” (NIV similar).
Or perhaps, “he triumphs over his enemies” (cf. NIV); NLT “will crush all his enemies.”

verses.zh: 我许久闭口不言，静默不语；现在我要喊叫，像产难的妇人；我要急气而喘哮。
verses.en: “I have been inactive[NOTE:1] for a long time;I kept quiet and held back.Like a woman in labor I groan;I pant and gasp.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “silent” (so NASB, NIV, TEV, NLT); CEV “have held my temper.”
The imagery depicts the Lord as a warrior who is eager to fight and can no longer hold himself back from the attack.

verses.zh: 我要使大山小冈变为荒场，使其上的花草都枯干；我要使江河变为洲岛，使水池都干涸。
verses.en: I will make the trees on the mountains and hills wither up;[NOTE:1] I will dry up all their vegetation.I will turn streams into islands[NOTE:2] and dry up pools of water.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I will dry up the mountains and hills.” The “mountains and hills” stand by synecdoche for the trees that grow on them. Some prefer to derive the verb from a homonymic root and translate, “I will lay waste.”

The Hebrew text reads, “I will turn streams into coastlands [or “islands”].” Scholars who believe that this reading makes little sense have proposed an emendation of אִיִּים (ʾiyyim, “islands”) to צִיּוֹת (tsiyyot, “dry places”; cf. NCV, NLT, TEV). However, since all the versions support the MT reading, there is insufficient grounds for an emendation here. Although the imagery of changing rivers into islands is somewhat strange, J. N. Oswalt describes this imagery against the backdrop of rivers of the Near East. The receding of these rivers at times occasioned the appearance of previously submerged islands (Isaiah [NICOT], 2:126).
The imagery of this verse, which depicts the Lord bringing a curse of infertility to the earth, metaphorically describes how the Lord will destroy his enemies.

verses.zh: 我要引瞎子行不认识的道，领他们走不知道的路；在他们面前使黑暗变为光明，使弯曲变为平直。这些事我都要行，并不离弃他们。
verses.en: I will lead the blind along an unfamiliar way;[NOTE:1] I will guide them down paths they have never traveled.[NOTE:2] I will turn the darkness in front of them into lightand level out the rough ground.[NOTE:3] This is what I will do for them.I will not abandon them.
notes: Heb “a way they do not know” (so NASB); NRSV “a road they do not know.”
Heb “in paths they do not know I will make them walk.”
Heb “and the rough ground into a level place.”

verses.zh: 倚靠雕刻的偶像，对铸造的偶像说：你是我们的神；这等人要退后，全然蒙羞。
verses.en: Those who trust in idolswill turn back and be utterly humiliated,[NOTE:1] those who say to metal images, ‘You are our gods.’
notes: Heb “be ashamed with shame”; ASV, NASB “be utterly put to shame.”

verses.zh: 你们这耳聋的，听吧！你们这眼瞎的，看吧！使你们能看见。
verses.en: “Listen, you deaf ones!Take notice,[NOTE:1] you blind ones!
notes: Heb “look to see”; NAB, NCV “look and see”; NRSV “look up and see.”

verses.zh: 谁比我的仆人眼瞎呢？谁比我差遣的使者耳聋呢？谁瞎眼像那与我和好的？谁瞎眼像耶和华的仆人呢？
verses.en: My servant is truly blind,my messenger is truly deaf.My covenant partner,[NOTE:1] the servant of the Lord, is truly blind.[NOTE:2]
notes: The precise meaning of מְשֻׁלָּם (meshullam) in this context is uncertain. In later biblical Hebrew the form (which appears to be a Pual participle from the root שָׁלַם, shalam) occurs as a proper name, Meshullam. The Pual of שָׁלַם (“be complete”) is attested with the meaning “repaid, requited,” but that makes little sense here. BDB 1023 s.v. שָׁלַם relates the form to the denominative verb שָׁלַם (“be at peace”) and paraphrases “one in a covenant of peace” (J. N. Oswalt suggests “the covenanted one”; Isaiah [NICOT], 2:128, n. 59) Some emend the form to מֹשְׁלָם (moshelam, “their ruler”) or to מְשֻׁלָּחִי (meshullakhi, “my sent [or “commissioned”] one”), which fits nicely in the parallelism (note “my messenger” in the previous line). The translation above assumes an emendation to כְּמוֹ שֹׁלְמִי (kemo sholemi, “like my ally”). Isaiah uses כְּמוֹ in 30:22 and perhaps 51:5; for שֹׁלְמי (“my ally”) see Ps 7:5 HT (7:4 ET).

Heb “Who is blind but my servant, and deaf like my messenger I send? Who is blind like my commissioned one, blind like the servant of the Lord?” The point of the rhetorical questions is that no one is as blind/deaf as this servant. In this context the Lord’s “servant” is exiled Israel (cf. 41:8-9), which is spiritually blind and deaf and has failed to fulfill God’s purpose for it. This servant stands in contrast to the ideal “Israel” of the servant songs.

verses.zh: 你看见许多事却不领会，耳朵开通却不听见。
verses.en: You see[NOTE:1] many things, but don’t comprehend;[NOTE:2] their ears are open, but do not hear.”
notes: The consonantal text (Kethib) has a perfect, second person masculine singular; the marginal reading (Qere) has an infinitive absolute, which functions here as a finite verb.
Heb “but you do not guard [i.e., retain in your memory]”; NIV11 “but you pay no attention.”

verses.zh: 耶和华因自己公义的缘故，喜欢使律法（或译：训诲）为大，为尊。
verses.en: The Lord wanted to exhibit his justiceby magnifying his law and displaying it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The Lord was pleased for the sake of his righteousness [or “justice”], he was magnifying [the] law and was making [it] glorious.” The Lord contrasts his good intentions for the people with their present crisis (v. 22). To demonstrate his just character and attract the nations, the Lord wanted to showcase his law among and through Israel (Deut 4:5-8). But Israel disobeyed (v. 24) and failed to carry out their commission.

verses.zh: 但这百姓是被抢被夺的，都牢笼在坑中，隐藏在狱里；他们作掠物，无人拯救，作掳物，无人说交还。
verses.en: But these people are looted and plundered;all of them are trapped in pits[NOTE:1] and held captive[NOTE:2] in prisons.They were carried away as loot with no one to rescue them;they were carried away as plunder, and no one says, “Bring that back!”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text has בַּחוּרִים (bakhurim, “young men”), but the text should be emended to בְּהוֹרִים (behorim, “in holes”).
Heb “and made to be hidden”; NAB, NASB, NIV, TEV “hidden away in prisons.”
Heb “they became loot, and there was no one rescuing, plunder, and there was no one saying, ‘Bring back’.”

verses.zh: 你们中间谁肯侧耳听此，谁肯留心而听，以防将来呢？
verses.en: Who among you will pay attention to this?Who will listen attentively in the future?[NOTE:1]
notes: The interrogative particle is understood in the second line by ellipsis (note the preceding line).

verses.zh: 谁将雅各交出当作掳物，将以色列交给抢夺的呢？岂不是耶和华吗？就是我们所得罪的那位。他们不肯遵行他的道，也不听从他的训诲。
verses.en: Who handed Jacob over to the robber?Who handed Israel over to the looters?[NOTE:1] Was it not the Lord, against whom we sinned?They refused to follow his commands;they disobeyed his law.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Who gave to the robber Jacob, and Israel to the looters?” In the first line the consonantal text (Kethib) has מְשׁוֹסֶה (meshoseh), a Polel participle from שָׁסָה (shasah, “plunder”). The marginal reading (Qere) is מְשִׁיסָּה (meshissah), a noun meaning “plunder.” In this case one could translate “Who handed Jacob over as plunder?”
Heb “they were not willing in his ways to walk, and they did not listen to his law.”

verses.zh: 所以，他将猛烈的怒气和争战的勇力倾倒在以色列的身上。在他四围如火着起，他还不知道，烧着他，他也不介意。
verses.en: So he poured out his fierce anger on them,[NOTE:1] along with the devastation[NOTE:2] of war.Its flames encircled them,[NOTE:3] but they did not realize it;[NOTE:4] it burned against them, but they did not take it to heart.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew third masculine singular pronoun, representing the nation, has been rendered as the third plural throughout this verse.
Heb “strength” (so KJV, NASB); NAB “fury”; NASB “fierceness”; NIV “violence.”
Heb “and it blazed against him all around.” The subject of the third feminine singular verb “blazed” is the divine חֵמָה (khemah, “anger”) mentioned in the previous line.
It is not that he did not know about the war, but he did not attribute this to God’s wrath.
Heb “but he did not set [it] upon [his] heart.” The Hebrew word “heart” also refers to the mind.
